title: "Street setup: drive graph, lane counts and SDOT ↔ OSM way-id repair"
author: "Stephen Siciliano"
output: html_document
params:
  # ---- inputs ----
  osm_pbf:                    "data/public/osm/washington-260122.osm.pbf"
  lanes_geojson:              "data/public/sdot/traffic_lanes.geojson"
  streets_geojson:            "data/public/sdot/seattle_streets.geojson"   # SDOT Seattle Streets (downloaded on first use)
  proposed_bus_lanes_geojson: "data/own/proposed_bus_lanes.geojson"
  snd_csv:                    "data/own/sdot_snd_osm_crosswalk.csv"
  corridors_csv:              "data/own/osm_snd_corridors.csv"
  # ---- outputs (outputs/streets/) ----
  streetnet_rds:              "outputs/streets/osm_streetnet.rds"     # driveable OSM ways, PSRC 4-county clip
  graph_rds:                  "outputs/streets/drive_graph.rds"       # routable dodgr graph
  street_grid_geojson:        "outputs/streets/street_grid.geojson"   # every Seattle street segment, all properties
  repair_csv:                 "outputs/streets/way_id_repair.csv"     # corridor-level fixes to the crosswalk
  # ---- Part 1: drive graph ----
  psrc_counties:  !r c("King", "Pierce", "Snohomish", "Kitsap")
  tigris_year:    2020
  wt_profile:     "motorcar"
  force_rebuild_streetnet: false
  force_rebuild_graph:     true
  # Sanity-check OSM way IDs that *must* be present (Magnolia's three bridges)
  smoke_test_way_ids: !r c("43032658", "22758987", "43314745")
  # ---- Part 3: way-id repair ----
  # Spatial parameters. Both sides are pre-filtered by name/ref to a single
  # corridor, so we can afford to be generous — a sample point on a long OSM
  # way will still find the right COMPKEY even if the nearest COMPKEY's
  # centroid is far away (because SND is much more subdivided).
  sample_spacing_m:     25
  # Maximum distance from an OSM sample point to its nearest in-corridor
  # COMPKEY. Acts as a safety net so a single stray OSM way that happens to
  # share a name but is geometrically off-corridor doesn't get attached.
  max_sample_dist_m:    300
  # Fallback maximum distance, applied only to OSM ways that produced ZERO
  # hits at the strict threshold above. The corridor name/ref filter has
  # already constrained the universe to the right road, so we accept
  # nearest snaps from much farther away rather than silently dropping the
  # way. Catches the SR-99 Tunnel (OSM follows the underground alignment,
  # SDOT draws street-level) and the Ship Canal Bridge (elevated alignment
  # vs surface footprint).
  max_sample_dist_fallback_m: 2000
  # CRS for planar geometry (UTM 10N covers PSRC).
  planar_crs:           32610
  # Default for cases where OSM oneway tag is missing/blank — treat as
  # two-way (matches OSM convention).
  default_oneway:       "no"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = FALSE)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf)
  library(tigris)
  library(osmextract)
  library(dodgr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(tidyr)
  library(stringr)
  library(purrr)
  library(httr)
  library(jsonlite)
  library(readr)
})

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
dir.create("outputs/streets", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

Builds everything later stages need to know about the street network, written
to `outputs/streets/`:

1. **Drive graph** (`osm_streetnet.rds`, `drive_graph.rds`) — the OpenStreetMap
   Washington extract clipped to the four PSRC counties, as an `sf` layer of
   driveable ways and as a routable `dodgr` graph. Every edge carries its OSM way
   id, which links road edges to SDOT street segments, traffic counts and lanes.
2. **Street grid** (`street_grid.geojson`) — every Seattle street segment (SDOT
   Seattle Streets) with its properties: current through-lane counts per
   direction, the lane counts after the proposed bus lanes, lane widths, and
   arterial / divided-carriageway / freeway-ramp flags.
3. **Way-id repair** (`way_id_repair.csv`) — corrected SDOT ↔ OSM way-id links
   on key corridors where the crosswalk (`data/own/sdot_snd_osm_crosswalk.csv`)
   is wrong or needs a many-to-many mapping per direction. Phase 2 overlays it on
   the crosswalk.

# Part 1 — Drive graph from OpenStreetMap

## 1. PSRC 4-county clip polygon

```{r psrc-polygon}
counties_wa <- tigris::counties(state = "WA",
                                year  = params$tigris_year,
                                class = "sf") |>
  sf::st_transform(4326) |>
  sf::st_make_valid()

psrc_sf <- counties_wa |>
  dplyr::filter(NAME %in% params$psrc_counties)

stopifnot(nrow(psrc_sf) == length(params$psrc_counties))
cat("PSRC counties loaded:", paste(sort(psrc_sf$NAME), collapse = ", "), "\n")

psrc_union <- sf::st_union(psrc_sf)
psrc_bbox  <- sf::st_bbox(psrc_union)
print(psrc_bbox)
```

## 2. Read & clip the PBF

We use `osmextract::oe_read` with a bbox spatial filter (`-spat`, much more
reliable across GDAL builds than `-clipsrc` polygon clipping), then
filter to driveable highway classes and clip to the exact PSRC polygon
in R afterward. We request the OSM tags `weight_streetnet` and downstream
code need (`lanes`, `maxspeed`, `oneway`, `bridge`, `tunnel`, `junction`,
`access`, `ref`) via `extra_tags` so they survive into the dodgr graph.

```{r read-pbf}
stopifnot(file.exists(params$osm_pbf))

drive_classes <- c(
  "motorway", "motorway_link", "trunk", "trunk_link",
  "primary",  "primary_link",  "secondary", "secondary_link",
  "tertiary", "tertiary_link", "unclassified",
  "residential", "living_street", "service"
)

if (!file.exists(params$streetnet_rds) ||
    isTRUE(params$force_rebuild_streetnet)) {

  # osmextract writes a .gpkg conversion next to the .osm.pbf it reads. Read a
  # hard link inside the cache so that file lands in cache/, not in data/.
  pbf_link <- file.path("cache", "osm", basename(params$osm_pbf))
  if (!file.exists(pbf_link) || file.info(pbf_link)$size != file.info(params$osm_pbf)$size) {
    dir.create(dirname(pbf_link), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    unlink(pbf_link)
    if (!isTRUE(file.link(params$osm_pbf, pbf_link))) file.copy(params$osm_pbf, pbf_link)
  }
  message("Reading PBF — first run will be slow (osmextract converts it to a ",
          ".gpkg in cache/osm/; subsequent reads are fast).")

  # PSRC bbox as an sfc polygon — used as a -spat filter (bbox, not polygon
  # clip). This widens slightly past the four counties at the corners but
  # we trim with an exact polygon intersect after the read.
  psrc_bbox_sfc <- sf::st_as_sfc(psrc_bbox, crs = 4326)

  t0 <- Sys.time()
  streetnet <- osmextract::oe_read(
    file_path     = normalizePath(pbf_link, winslash = "/"),
    layer         = "lines",
    boundary      = psrc_bbox_sfc,
    boundary_type = "spat",
    extra_tags    = c("lanes", "maxspeed", "oneway", "bridge", "tunnel",
                      "junction", "access", "ref", "service"),
    quiet         = FALSE
  )
  cat(sprintf("Read %d LineStrings (bbox filter) in %.1fs\n",
              nrow(streetnet),
              as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")))

  # Filter to driveable highway tags. (`oe_read` returns rows with NA
  # `highway` for non-road lines like waterways, paths, etc.)
  streetnet <- streetnet |>
    dplyr::filter(highway %in% drive_classes)
  cat("After highway filter:", nrow(streetnet), "features\n")

  # Trim to the exact PSRC 4-county polygon. `st_filter` with the default
  # `st_intersects` predicate keeps any LineString that touches PSRC; this
  # is what we want (a highway crossing the boundary stays in).
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  streetnet <- sf::st_filter(streetnet, psrc_union,
                             .predicate = sf::st_intersects)
  cat(sprintf("After PSRC polygon intersect: %d features (%.1fs)\n",
              nrow(streetnet),
              as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")))

  saveRDS(streetnet, params$streetnet_rds)
  message("Saved streetnet cache: ", normalizePath(params$streetnet_rds))
} else {
  streetnet <- readRDS(params$streetnet_rds)
  cat("Loaded cached streetnet:", nrow(streetnet), "features\n")
}

# osm_id is always populated by osmextract; double-check anyway.
n_missing <- sum(is.na(streetnet$osm_id))
cat(sprintf("Features with NA osm_id: %d (%.4f%%)\n",
            n_missing, 100 * mean(is.na(streetnet$osm_id))))
if (n_missing > 0) {
  stop("Some features lack osm_id — weight_streetnet would assign NA way_id.")
}

cat("Highway-class breakdown:\n")
hwy_counts <- streetnet |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  dplyr::count(highway, sort = TRUE) |>
  as.data.frame()
print(hwy_counts, row.names = FALSE)
```

## 3. Build the dodgr graph

```{r build-graph}
if (!file.exists(params$graph_rds) || isTRUE(params$force_rebuild_graph)) {

  message("Weighting streetnet for ", params$wt_profile, " ...")
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  graph <- dodgr::weight_streetnet(
    x          = streetnet,
    wt_profile = params$wt_profile,
    id_col     = "osm_id",
    # `oneway` is consumed by weight_streetnet to decide whether to create
    # a reverse edge, but we keep it as an explicit column too — downstream
    # capacity / SND-mapping logic uses it as a fallback when the SND
    # ONEWAY flag is missing or contradicts the OSM tag.
    keep_cols  = c("bridge", "tunnel", "ref", "name", "maxspeed", "lanes",
                   "oneway")
  )
  cat(sprintf("Weighted in %.1fs — edges: %d\n",
              as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs"),
              nrow(graph)))

  # Critical invariant: every edge carries the OSM way ID it came from.
  na_way <- sum(is.na(graph$way_id))
  cat(sprintf("Edges with NA way_id (post-weight): %d (%.4f%%)\n",
              na_way, 100 * mean(is.na(graph$way_id))))
  if (na_way > 0) {
    stop("weight_streetnet produced edges without way_id — abort. ",
         "Inspect head(graph[is.na(graph$way_id), ]) to see which.")
  }

  # Largest connected component (matches behavior of original cache).
  message("Filtering to component == 1 ...")
  graph <- graph[!is.na(graph$component) & graph$component == 1, ]
  cat("After component=1 filter:", nrow(graph), "edges\n")
  cat("Distinct OSM way_ids in graph:",
      length(unique(graph$way_id)), "\n")

  saveRDS(graph, params$graph_rds)
  message("Saved: ", normalizePath(params$graph_rds))
} else {
  graph <- readRDS(params$graph_rds)
  cat("Loaded cached graph:", nrow(graph), "edges\n")
}
```

## 4. Smoke test — verify the Magnolia bridges are present by way_id

```{r smoke-test}
hits <- tibble::tibble(
  way_id = params$smoke_test_way_ids,
  n_edges_in_graph = vapply(params$smoke_test_way_ids, function(b) {
    sum(as.character(graph$way_id) == b, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, integer(1))
)
print(hits)

if (any(hits$n_edges_in_graph == 0)) {
  warning("Some smoke-test OSM ways are missing from the graph. ",
          "Check that the PSRC clip polygon covers the bridge location, ",
          "and that the bridge's highway class is in `drive_classes`.")
} else {
  cat("All smoke-test bridges found in graph ✓\n")
}

# Spot-check geometry: print one edge per bridge and its midpoint.
for (b in params$smoke_test_way_ids) {
  rows <- which(as.character(graph$way_id) == b)
  if (length(rows) == 0) next
  r <- rows[1]
  cat(sprintf(
    "  way_id %s: %d edges | sample edge midpoint (%.5f, %.5f) | highway=%s\n",
    b, length(rows),
    (graph$from_lat[r] + graph$to_lat[r]) / 2,
    (graph$from_lon[r] + graph$to_lon[r]) / 2,
    graph$highway[r]))
}
```

# Part 2 — Lane counts, current and with bus lanes

Build a per-segment table of through-lane counts for every Seattle street
segment, with a "new" count for the subset of segments slated for bus lanes.

Inputs:

* **Seattle Streets** — ArcGIS REST FeatureServer, downloaded fresh:
  https://services.arcgis.com/ZOyb2t4B0UYuYNYH/arcgis/rest/services/Seattle_Streets_1/FeatureServer/0
  Used as the spatial base. Joins via `COMPKEY` (= `SEGKEY` in the lanes data)
  and `SEGDIR`.
* `data/public/sdot/traffic_lanes.geojson` — one feature per individual lane,
  often split mid-block. Fields: `SEGKEY`, `LANEKEY`, `TRAFFDIR`, `LANETYPE`,
  `DISTANCE`, `ENDDISTANC`, `OPERENDDAT`.
* `data/own/proposed_bus_lanes.geojson` — proposed bus-lane segments
  (one row per block-segment getting a *pair* of bus lanes). The only fields
  pulled in are `LaneWidthsSummary.csv.MinWidth` (-> `MinWidth`),
  `LaneWidthsSummary.csv.WidthOpptyMin` (-> `MinOppty`), and
  `LaneWidthsSummary.csv.WidthOpptyMax` (-> `MaxOppty`).

Output:

* `outputs/streets/street_grid.geojson` — every Seattle street segment, with current
  per-direction through-lane counts (`SAMELANECOUNT` aligned to `SEGDIR`,
  `OPSLANECOUNT` opposing); `MinWidth`/`MinOppty`/`MaxOppty` where available;
  and `NEW_SAMELANECOUNT` / `NEW_OPSLANECOUNT` for segments with a proposed
  bus lane (NA otherwise).

```{r lane-constants}
# SND_SEGMENT_TYPE code for freeway ramps. Bus-lane proposals overlapping
# a ramp COMPKEY are forced back to current lane counts (no capacity change).
RAMP_SEGMENT_TYPE <- 4L

STREETS_URL <- "https://services.arcgis.com/ZOyb2t4B0UYuYNYH/arcgis/rest/services/Seattle_Streets_1/FeatureServer/0/query"
```



## 1. Download Seattle Streets (paginated)

The FeatureServer caps response size, so we page with `resultOffset` until the
server tells us there's nothing more. Cached to disk so re-knits are fast;
delete `data/public/sdot/seattle_streets.geojson` to force a refresh.

```{r download-streets}
fetch_streets <- function(url, page_size = 2000) {
  out <- list()
  offset <- 0
  repeat {
    q <- list(
      where = "1=1",
      outFields = "*",
      f = "geojson",
      outSR = 4326,
      resultOffset = offset,
      resultRecordCount = page_size
    )
    r <- httr::GET(url, query = q, httr::timeout(120))
    httr::stop_for_status(r)
    txt <- httr::content(r, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8")

    # Read this page as sf
    page <- sf::st_read(txt, quiet = TRUE)
    if (nrow(page) == 0) break
    out[[length(out) + 1]] <- page

    # Some servers signal more via exceededTransferLimit at the JSON root.
    j <- jsonlite::fromJSON(txt, simplifyVector = FALSE)
    more <- isTRUE(j$exceededTransferLimit) ||
            isTRUE(j$properties$exceededTransferLimit)
    if (!more && nrow(page) < page_size) break
    offset <- offset + nrow(page)
    cat("  fetched", offset, "features\n")
  }
  do.call(rbind, out)
}

if (!file.exists(params$streets_geojson)) {
  message("Downloading Seattle Streets...")
  streets_dl <- fetch_streets(STREETS_URL)
  dir.create(dirname(params$streets_geojson), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  if (file.exists(params$streets_geojson)) file.remove(params$streets_geojson)
  st_write(streets_dl, params$streets_geojson, driver = "GeoJSON", quiet = TRUE)
}

streets <- st_read(params$streets_geojson, quiet = TRUE)
cat("Seattle Streets:", nrow(streets), "features\n")
cat("columns:", paste(names(streets), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 2. Load + filter the lane inventory

Drop lanes with a non-null `OPERENDDAT` (decommissioned). `TRAFFDIR == "C"` is
the bidirectional center turn lane and is excluded from directional counting.

```{r load-lanes}
lanes <- st_read(params$lanes_geojson, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(is.na(OPERENDDAT) | OPERENDDAT == "") %>%
  filter(!is.na(SEGKEY), !is.na(TRAFFDIR), !is.na(LANETYPE)) %>%
  filter(TRAFFDIR != "C")

cat("kept", nrow(lanes), "active directional lane features\n")
```

## 3. Through-lane counter

* `T1..T5` are parallel through lanes — count distinct T-numbers.
* `TRT` / `TLT` substitute for `T1`.
* Everything else (turn-only, BUS*, HOV, parking, etc.) doesn't add capacity.

```{r count-fn}
THROUGH_TYPES <- c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4", "T5")

# TRT (Through-Right Turn) and TLT (Through-Left Turn) are physical
# through-lanes that also permit turns at the next intersection — count
# them as the equivalent of T1.
#
# TSHRW is a through-lane with a sharrow (bike-share marking). The lane
# still operates as a regular travel lane for cars; the sharrow is paint,
# not lane geometry. Wallingford Ave N and several other "sharrowed
# arterials" are 0/0 in the inventory under the old logic because their
# only travel lanes are marked TSHRW. Treat them as T1.
TRAVEL_ALIASES <- c("TRT", "TLT", "TSHRW")

count_through <- function(lanetype) {
  lt <- ifelse(lanetype %in% TRAVEL_ALIASES, "T1", lanetype)
  lt <- lt[lt %in% THROUGH_TYPES]
  length(unique(lt))
}
```

## 4. Per-(SEGKEY, TRAFFDIR) start / end counts

For each (SEGKEY, TRAFFDIR):

* **start** = lanes at the minimum `DISTANCE` value present.
* **end**   = lanes at the maximum `ENDDISTANC` value present.

Reported lane count = `min(start, end)` (bottleneck), with both kept for
inspection.

```{r start-end-counts}
seg_dir_counts <- lanes %>%
  group_by(SEGKEY, TRAFFDIR) %>%
  summarise(
    .groups = "drop",
    min_dist = min(DISTANCE, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_end  = max(ENDDISTANC, na.rm = TRUE),
    start_lanes = count_through(LANETYPE[DISTANCE  == min_dist[1]]),
    end_lanes   = count_through(LANETYPE[ENDDISTANC == max_end[1]])
  ) %>%
  mutate(lane_count = pmin(start_lanes, end_lanes)) %>%
  select(SEGKEY, TRAFFDIR, lane_count, start_lanes, end_lanes)

head(seg_dir_counts)
```

## 5. Direction helper + join lane counts onto streets

```{r dir-helper}
opposite_dir <- function(d) {
  d <- toupper(d)
  recode(d,
    "N"  = "S",  "S"  = "N",
    "E"  = "W",  "W"  = "E",
    "NE" = "SW", "SW" = "NE",
    "NW" = "SE", "SE" = "NW",
    .default = NA_character_
  )
}
```

Seattle Streets exposes the segment id as `COMPKEY` and the orientation as
`SEGDIR`. We treat `SEGDIR` as the SAME side and its opposite as OPS.

```{r join-counts}
streets <- streets %>%
  mutate(
    COMPKEY = as.integer(COMPKEY),
    SEGDIR = toupper(trimws(as.character(SEGDIR))),
    OPPDIR = opposite_dir(SEGDIR)
  )

same_join <- seg_dir_counts %>%
  rename(TRAFFDIR_SAME = TRAFFDIR,
         SAMELANECOUNT_ARTERIAL = lane_count,
         SAME_START = start_lanes,
         SAME_END   = end_lanes)

ops_join <- seg_dir_counts %>%
  rename(TRAFFDIR_OPS = TRAFFDIR,
         OPSLANECOUNT_ARTERIAL = lane_count,
         OPS_START = start_lanes,
         OPS_END   = end_lanes)

streets_joined <- streets %>%
  left_join(same_join, by = c("COMPKEY" = "SEGKEY", "SEGDIR" = "TRAFFDIR_SAME")) %>%
  left_join(ops_join,  by = c("COMPKEY" = "SEGKEY", "OPPDIR" = "TRAFFDIR_OPS"))
```

## 6. Apply residential defaults for current counts

A segment is treated as non-arterial / residential when neither direction is
present in the lane inventory. Default to 1 lane each direction.

> **TODO / caveat:** we cannot detect residential one-way streets from this
> data alone — those should be 1/0 not 1/1. Splice in a one-way flag here if
> one becomes available.

```{r residential-defaults}
# Freeway-class COMPKEYs (I-5, I-90, SR-99 mainline, SR-520) are WSDOT-
# maintained and not in SDOT's lane inventory, so `is_arterial=FALSE` for
# them — but the residential default of 1+1 lanes is obviously wrong. We
# emit NA instead; the downstream consumer (`safe_current` in
# Phase2RunSimulation §5)
# treats NA as a fallback trigger and picks up the OSM `lanes` tag, which
# is correct per-direction for the OSM-tagged-oneway freeway features.
FREEWAY_ARTDESCRIPTS <- c("Interstate/Freeway", "State Route/Freeway")

streets_joined <- streets_joined %>%
  mutate(
    is_arterial = !is.na(SAMELANECOUNT_ARTERIAL) | !is.na(OPSLANECOUNT_ARTERIAL),
    is_freeway_class_no_data = !is_arterial &
                               as.character(ARTDESCRIPT) %in% FREEWAY_ARTDESCRIPTS,
    SAMELANECOUNT = case_when(
      is_arterial               ~ coalesce(SAMELANECOUNT_ARTERIAL, 0L),
      is_freeway_class_no_data  ~ NA_integer_,
      TRUE                      ~ 1L),
    OPSLANECOUNT = case_when(
      is_arterial               ~ coalesce(OPSLANECOUNT_ARTERIAL,  0L),
      is_freeway_class_no_data  ~ NA_integer_,
      TRUE                      ~ 1L)
  )

cat("COMPKEYs with freeway-class but no SDOT lane data (using OSM fallback):",
    sum(streets_joined$is_freeway_class_no_data, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

# ---- Baseline sanity floor ----
# 2-way roads physically must have ≥ 1 through-lane in each direction;
# 1-way roads must have ≥ 1 in the flow direction. SDOT's inventory
# under-counts in two known cases — sharrow-only blocks (the TSHRW
# category, which the original code didn't recognise) and arterial
# segments where every lane is marked turn-only — both of which produce
# SAMELANECOUNT=0 and/or OPSLANECOUNT=0 for streets that obviously have
# through traffic. The floor here corrects those without touching:
#   * residential streets (already get the 1/1 default above);
#   * freeway-no-data (stays NA, OSM-fallback handles it);
#   * legitimate 1-way streets (only the flow-aligned direction gets
#     floored, the reverse direction correctly stays 0).
streets_joined <- streets_joined %>%
  mutate(
    .is_one_way_road   = toupper(trimws(as.character(ONEWAY))) == "Y",
    .flow_dir          = toupper(trimws(as.character(ONEWAYDIR))),
    .seg_dir           = toupper(trimws(as.character(SEGDIR))),
    .same_is_flow_side = .is_one_way_road & .flow_dir == .seg_dir &
                         nzchar(.flow_dir),
    .ops_is_flow_side  = .is_one_way_road & .flow_dir != .seg_dir &
                         nzchar(.flow_dir),
    # Compute the floor (integer scalar broadcast) and pmax against current.
    # Both inputs to pmax are guaranteed integer vectors of the same length,
    # so no type-inference oddities can turn the column into a list.
    .same_floor = dplyr::case_when(
      !.is_one_way_road                  ~ 1L,
      .same_is_flow_side                 ~ 1L,
      TRUE                               ~ 0L),
    .ops_floor = dplyr::case_when(
      !.is_one_way_road                  ~ 1L,
      .ops_is_flow_side                  ~ 1L,
      TRUE                               ~ 0L),
    # NA propagates: pmax(NA, x) is NA, so freeway-no-data stays NA.
    SAMELANECOUNT = pmax(as.integer(SAMELANECOUNT), .same_floor),
    OPSLANECOUNT  = pmax(as.integer(OPSLANECOUNT),  .ops_floor)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-.is_one_way_road, -.flow_dir, -.seg_dir,
                -.same_is_flow_side, -.ops_is_flow_side,
                -.same_floor, -.ops_floor)

cat(sprintf("After baseline sanity floor: %d COMPKEYs with SAMELANECOUNT>=1, %d with OPSLANECOUNT>=1\n",
            sum(streets_joined$SAMELANECOUNT >= 1L, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(streets_joined$OPSLANECOUNT >= 1L, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

## 6b. Detect divided-road carriageways

A divided arterial (Beacon Ave S, I-5, etc.) is encoded in SND as **two
adjacent one-way COMPKEYs** going opposite directions. A proposed bus
lane on such a corridor takes **one** lane from each carriageway — not a
pair. The `new_through()` function below otherwise assumes every proposed
bus lane is a pair (10.5 ft + 10.5 ft = 21 ft), which double-penalises
divided corridors (4 lanes removed where 2 is correct).

We flag a COMPKEY as `is_divided_carriageway` when it's `ONEWAY = Y` and
there's another `ONEWAY = Y` COMPKEY within `PAIR_BUFFER_M` going the
opposite `ONEWAYDIR`. Standalone one-way streets (downtown 1st/2nd Ave)
have no paired carriageway nearby and keep the pair-of-bus-lanes
treatment — those streets are proposed to be converted to two-way for the
bus lanes, so the pair logic matches the intent.

```{r divided-detection}
PAIR_BUFFER_M <- 50

oneways <- streets %>%
  filter(toupper(trimws(as.character(ONEWAY))) == "Y") %>%
  mutate(.dir_norm = toupper(trimws(as.character(ONEWAYDIR)))) %>%
  filter(.dir_norm %in% c("N","S","E","W","NE","NW","SE","SW"))

cat("One-way COMPKEYs:", nrow(oneways), "\n")

if (nrow(oneways) > 0) {
  # Project to a planar CRS (WA State Plane North or UTM 10N) so the
  # within-distance check is in metres rather than degrees.
  oneways_p <- sf::st_transform(oneways, 32610)
  nearby <- sf::st_is_within_distance(oneways_p, oneways_p,
                                      dist = PAIR_BUFFER_M)

  is_divided <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(oneways_p)), function(i) {
    this_dir <- oneways_p$.dir_norm[i]
    opp <- opposite_dir(this_dir)
    others <- setdiff(nearby[[i]], i)
    if (!length(others)) return(FALSE)
    any(oneways_p$.dir_norm[others] == opp, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, logical(1))

  divided_compkeys <- oneways_p$COMPKEY[is_divided]
  cat("Divided-road carriageway COMPKEYs:", length(divided_compkeys), "\n")
} else {
  divided_compkeys <- integer(0)
}

streets_joined <- streets_joined %>%
  mutate(is_divided_carriageway = COMPKEY %in% divided_compkeys)
```

## 6c. Detect freeway ramps

Bus-lane proposals don't apply to on/off ramps — they're short, geometrically
constrained, and lane configuration is dictated by the upstream/downstream
mainline. Flag ramps so `NEW_SAMELANECOUNT` / `NEW_OPSLANECOUNT` get forced
back to the current values (no capacity change).

Detection uses `SND_SEGMENT_TYPE = 4` (SDOT's authoritative ramp code) by
COMPKEY. The SND CSV has one row per `(COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR)`;
`SND_SEGMENT_TYPE` is constant per COMPKEY so we just take the first
non-NA value per COMPKEY.

```{r ramp-detection}
snd_seg_type_by_compkey <- readr::read_csv(
    params$snd_csv,
    col_select = c("COMPKEY", "SND_SEGMENT_TYPE"),
    col_types  = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),
    progress   = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(COMPKEY = suppressWarnings(as.integer(COMPKEY)),
         SND_SEGMENT_TYPE = suppressWarnings(as.integer(SND_SEGMENT_TYPE))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(COMPKEY)) %>%
  group_by(COMPKEY) %>%
  summarise(SND_SEGMENT_TYPE = {
              v <- SND_SEGMENT_TYPE[!is.na(SND_SEGMENT_TYPE)]
              if (length(v)) v[1] else NA_integer_
            },
            .groups = "drop")

streets_joined <- streets_joined %>%
  left_join(snd_seg_type_by_compkey, by = "COMPKEY") %>%
  mutate(is_freeway_ramp = !is.na(SND_SEGMENT_TYPE) &
                           SND_SEGMENT_TYPE == RAMP_SEGMENT_TYPE)

cat("Freeway ramp COMPKEYs flagged:",
    sum(streets_joined$is_freeway_ramp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
```

## 7. Pull MinWidth / MinOppty / MaxOppty from the proposed bus lanes

Most Seattle Streets segments aren't in this file; they get NA.

```{r transit-widths}
transit <- st_read(params$proposed_bus_lanes_geojson, quiet = TRUE) %>% st_drop_geometry()

seg_col      <- grep("COMPKEY",      names(transit), value = TRUE)[1]
minw_col     <- grep("MinWidth",     names(transit), value = TRUE)[1]
minopp_col   <- grep("WidthOpptyMin", names(transit), value = TRUE)[1]
maxopp_col   <- grep("WidthOpptyMax", names(transit), value = TRUE)[1]
stopifnot(!is.na(seg_col), !is.na(minw_col), !is.na(minopp_col), !is.na(maxopp_col))

transit_widths <- transit %>%
  transmute(
    COMPKEY  = as.integer(.data[[seg_col]]),
    MinWidth = as.numeric(.data[[minw_col]]),
    MinOppty = as.numeric(.data[[minopp_col]]),
    MaxOppty = as.numeric(.data[[maxopp_col]])
  ) %>%
  # Collapse to one row per COMPKEY in case of duplicates
  group_by(COMPKEY) %>%
  summarise(
    MinWidth = min(MinWidth, na.rm = TRUE),
    MinOppty = min(MinOppty, na.rm = TRUE),
    MaxOppty = max(MaxOppty, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(MinWidth, MinOppty, MaxOppty),
                ~ if_else(is.infinite(.), NA_real_, .)))

streets_joined <- streets_joined %>%
  left_join(transit_widths, by = "COMPKEY") %>%
  mutate(has_proposed_bus_lane = !is.na(MinWidth))

# Freeway ramps are excluded from bus-lane impact entirely, regardless of
# whether they happen to fall inside a proposed bus-lane corridor
# polygon. Setting `has_proposed_bus_lane = FALSE` here makes the
# downstream `case_when` send NEW_* to NA (no change) and §5 of
# Phase2RunSimulation skip the priority-cap reduction for these
# COMPKEYs. We do this AFTER the join so MinWidth/MinOppty stay in the
# output for inspection. Note: §6c must have already run to populate
# `is_freeway_ramp`; the chunk order in this notebook is §6 → §6b → §6c
# → §7 → §8, so it's already there by the time we get here.
if ("is_freeway_ramp" %in% names(streets_joined)) {
  n_ramp_proposed <- sum(streets_joined$is_freeway_ramp &
                         streets_joined$has_proposed_bus_lane, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_ramp_proposed > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("Excluding %d freeway-ramp COMPKEYs from bus-lane impact\n",
                n_ramp_proposed))
  }
  streets_joined <- streets_joined %>%
    mutate(has_proposed_bus_lane = has_proposed_bus_lane &
                                   !coalesce(is_freeway_ramp, FALSE))
}
```

## 8. New through-lane counts (only where a bus lane is proposed)

Each row in `proposed_bus_lanes.geojson` is a *pair* of new bus lanes (one per
direction); `SEGDIR` is street orientation, not a flow direction. We don't
blindly subtract because parking, bike lanes, medians, and turn pockets can be
reallocated to through use. Decision is driven by `MinWidth` under aggressive
10-ft lanes:

| Min width (ft) | Width-based through-lane proposal                            |
|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `< 30`         | 0 / 0 (no through capacity could fit alongside a pair of 10-ft bus lanes) |
| `30 –< 40`     | 1 in one direction (priority: more current lanes; tie -> SEGDIR), 0 in the other |
| `40 –< 60`     | 1 per direction (capped by current; one-way stays one-way)   |
| `>= 60`        | Retain current, capped by `floor((width − 21) / 10)` total, distributed by current ratios |

**Sanity bound on NEW lanes**: `new ∈ [max(0, current − 1), current]` per
direction. Two pieces:
- upper bound `new ≤ current` — a bus-lane proposal can only remove lanes.
- lower bound `new ≥ current − 1` — at most one through-lane removed per
  direction. So `current = 1 → new ∈ {0, 1}` (the one lane may be lost),
  `current = 2 → new ∈ {1, 2}` (can't drop to 0), etc.

This is *not* a "minimum 1 lane" floor — when `current = 1`, new = 0 is
fully allowed, which is what happens on a narrow street that genuinely
can't fit any through-lane alongside the bus lane. The defense against
pathologically-low `current` values is the **baseline sanity floor**
applied earlier in §6: 2-way roads start with ≥ 1 each direction, 1-way
roads with ≥ 1 in the flow direction. So `new = 0` always means "we
genuinely lost the one through lane we had".

For non-arterial segments with a proposed bus lane, both sides collapse to 0
(one shared lane retained for local access).

**Divided-road carriageways** (Beacon Ave S, I-5, etc. — detected in §6b
as paired one-way COMPKEYs going opposite directions) use a separate
"single bus lane" logic, since only one bus lane is added per carriageway
(the other goes on the paired carriageway, a different COMPKEY). The
thresholds are halved relative to the pair logic:

| Min width (ft) | Through lanes outcome (divided carriageway)           |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `< 20`         | 0 (local access only)                                 |
| `20 –< 30`     | 1                                                     |
| `>= 30`        | Retain current, capped by `floor((width − 10.5) /9.5)`  |

Standalone one-way streets without a paired carriageway nearby (e.g.
downtown 1st/2nd Ave) keep the standard pair logic above — the intent
on those streets is to convert them to two-way at the time the bus lanes
go in.

```{r new-count-fn}
new_through <- function(width, same_cur, ops_cur, same_priority = TRUE,
                        is_divided = FALSE) {
  if (is.na(width)) return(c(NA_integer_, NA_integer_))
  same_cur <- as.integer(same_cur); ops_cur <- as.integer(ops_cur)
  # NA lane counts (freeway-class COMPKEYs without SDOT data) can't be
  # reasoned about for bus-lane impact — return NA so downstream skips
  # the capacity reduction and leaves OSM-derived lanes alone.
  if (is.na(same_cur) && is.na(ops_cur)) return(c(NA_integer_, NA_integer_))
  if (is.na(same_cur)) same_cur <- 0L
  if (is.na(ops_cur))  ops_cur  <- 0L

  width_based <- if (isTRUE(is_divided)) {
    # ---- Divided-road carriageway: single bus lane added to THIS carriageway
    # only (the other half lives on the paired carriageway, a different
    # COMPKEY). Thresholds are halved vs the pair logic (10 ft / 1 lane
    # instead of 20 ft / 2 lanes).
    same_branch <- same_cur > 0
    eff_cur <- if (same_branch) same_cur else ops_cur
    if (width < 20) {
      c(0L, 0L)
    } else if (width < 30) {
      if (same_branch) c(1L, 0L) else c(0L, 1L)
    } else {
      avail <- as.integer(floor((width - 10) / 10))   # reserve 10 ft for bus
      new <- as.integer(min(eff_cur, avail))
      if (same_branch) c(new, 0L) else c(0L, new)
    }
  } else if (width < 30) {
    # ---- Standard pair-of-bus-lanes logic ----
    c(0L, 0L)
  } else if (width < 40) {
    if (same_cur == 0 && ops_cur >  0) {
      c(0L, 1L)
    } else if (ops_cur  == 0 && same_cur > 0) {
      c(1L, 0L)
    } else if (same_cur > ops_cur) {
      c(1L, 0L)
    } else if (ops_cur  > same_cur) {
      c(0L, 1L)
    } else if (same_priority) {
      c(1L, 0L)
    } else {
      c(0L, 1L)
    }
  } else {
    avail <- as.integer(floor((width - 21) / 9.5))
    s <- 0L; o <- 0L
    if (avail > 0 && same_cur > 0) { s <- 1L; avail <- avail - 1L }
    if (avail > 0 && ops_cur  > 0) { o <- 1L; avail <- avail - 1L }
    while (avail > 0 && (s < same_cur || o < ops_cur)) {
      same_room <- s < same_cur
      ops_room  <- o < ops_cur
      if (same_room && !ops_room) {
        s <- s + 1L
      } else if (ops_room && !same_room) {
        o <- o + 1L
      } else {
        same_gap <- same_cur - s
        ops_gap  <- ops_cur  - o
        if (same_gap > ops_gap) {
          s <- s + 1L
        } else if (ops_gap > same_gap) {
          o <- o + 1L
        } else {
          if (same_priority) s <- s + 1L else o <- o + 1L
        }
      }
      avail <- avail - 1L
    }
    c(s, o)
  }

  # ---- Sanity bound: new ∈ [max(0, current − 1), current] per direction ----
  # Two pieces:
  #   * upper bound `new ≤ current` — a bus-lane proposal can only remove
  #     lanes, never add.
  #   * lower bound `new ≥ current − 1` — at most one lane removed per
  #     direction. This is NOT "minimum 1 lane" (which would block 0
  #     outcomes entirely); it's "minimum current − 1". So:
  #       current = 0 → new = 0 (no traffic in this direction; nothing to remove)
  #       current = 1 → new ∈ {0, 1}    (the one through lane may be lost)
  #       current = 2 → new ∈ {1, 2}    (lose at most 1)
  #       current = 3 → new ∈ {2, 3}    (lose at most 1)
  #   * floor at 0 to keep values non-negative.
  # The baseline sanity floor applied earlier in §6 guarantees current ≥ 1
  # in each through direction (2-way: both; 1-way: flow direction), so
  # `current − 1` is well-defined and ≥ 0 in practice.
  new_same <- min(max(width_based[1], same_cur - 1L, 0L), same_cur)
  new_ops  <- min(max(width_based[2], ops_cur  - 1L, 0L), ops_cur)
  c(as.integer(new_same), as.integer(new_ops))
}
```

```{r new-counts}
new_pairs <- purrr::pmap(
  list(streets_joined$MinWidth,
       streets_joined$SAMELANECOUNT,
       streets_joined$OPSLANECOUNT,
       streets_joined$is_divided_carriageway),
  function(w, s, o, d) new_through(w, s, o,
                                   same_priority = TRUE,
                                   is_divided = isTRUE(d))
)

streets_joined <- streets_joined %>%
  mutate(
    NEW_SAMELANECOUNT = vapply(new_pairs, `[`, integer(1), 1),
    NEW_OPSLANECOUNT  = vapply(new_pairs, `[`, integer(1), 2),
    # Residential override (only when there's actually a proposed bus lane)
    NEW_SAMELANECOUNT = case_when(
      !has_proposed_bus_lane ~ NA_integer_,
      !is_arterial           ~ 0L,
      TRUE                   ~ NEW_SAMELANECOUNT
    ),
    NEW_OPSLANECOUNT = case_when(
      !has_proposed_bus_lane ~ NA_integer_,
      !is_arterial           ~ 0L,
      TRUE                   ~ NEW_OPSLANECOUNT
    ),
    # Freeway ramps: any bus-lane proposal that happens to overlap a ramp
    # COMPKEY is forced back to current lane counts (no capacity change).
    # Ramps are short, geometrically constrained, and lane structure is set
    # by upstream/downstream mainline — they aren't a place to add or
    # subtract a through-lane for a bus lane.
    NEW_SAMELANECOUNT = if_else(is_freeway_ramp & has_proposed_bus_lane,
                                SAMELANECOUNT, NEW_SAMELANECOUNT),
    NEW_OPSLANECOUNT  = if_else(is_freeway_ramp & has_proposed_bus_lane,
                                OPSLANECOUNT,  NEW_OPSLANECOUNT)
  )
```

## 10. Write the output

```{r write}
dir.create(dirname(params$street_grid_geojson), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

out <- streets_joined %>%
  select(
    COMPKEY, SEGDIR, OPPDIR,
    is_arterial, has_proposed_bus_lane,
    is_divided_carriageway, is_freeway_ramp,
    SAMELANECOUNT, OPSLANECOUNT,
    NEW_SAMELANECOUNT, NEW_OPSLANECOUNT,
    MinWidth, MinOppty, MaxOppty,
    SAME_START, SAME_END, OPS_START, OPS_END,
    everything()
  )

if (file.exists(params$street_grid_geojson)) file.remove(params$street_grid_geojson)
st_write(out, params$street_grid_geojson, driver = "GeoJSON", quiet = TRUE)
cat("wrote", nrow(out), "features to", params$street_grid_geojson, "\n")
```

# Part 3 — SDOT ↔ OSM way-id repair

## Why this part

The canonical SND ↔ OSM map ([`sdot_snd_osm_crosswalk.csv`](data/own/sdot_snd_osm_crosswalk.csv)) was built by a separate spatial-match of SDOT street segments to OSM ways and is occasionally wrong on key corridors. The map collapses to one OSM way per SND_ID, which is also wrong in two specific cases:

1. **OSM-divided / SND-unified** (e.g. Aurora, Lake City Way). OSM treats the divided highway as two `oneway=yes` features; SND treats it as one COMPKEY with two `TRAFFICDIR` rows. The correct mapping is `way_id_NB → (..., TRAFFICDIR=N)`, `way_id_SB → (..., TRAFFICDIR=S)` — a many-to-many on the SND_ID.
2. **SND-divided** (e.g. Beacon Ave S). SND splits into two COMPKEYs/SND_IDs (NB and SB); OSM is usually two `oneway=yes` features as well. The correct mapping is `way_id_NB → (COMPKEY_NB, SND_ID_NB, N)`, etc.

This part produces [`outputs/streets/way_id_repair.csv`](outputs/streets/way_id_repair.csv) with columns `COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR, WAY_IDS` (comma-separated). Downstream, [`Phase2RunSimulation.Rmd`](Phase2RunSimulation.Rmd) §4c overlays it on the raw mapping (anti-join on the `(COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR)` triple, then bind).

## 1. Load the corridor list

The CSV gives a per-corridor filter: `osm_names` matches OSM `name`, `osm_refs` matches OSM `ref` (split on `;` if multi-valued), `snd_ordstnameconcats` matches SND `SND_ORD_STNAME_CONCAT`. Each cell is a comma-separated list; corridors with name changes (e.g. SR-99 → "AURORA AVE N", "AURORA BR", "SR99 TUNNEL NB", …) collect them in one row.

```{r load-corridors}
corridors_raw <- readr::read_csv(params$corridors_csv,
                                 show_col_types = FALSE,
                                 progress = FALSE) |>
  mutate(corridor_idx = row_number())

split_clean <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return(character(0))
  toupper(stringr::str_trim(strsplit(as.character(x), ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]))
}

corridors <- corridors_raw |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    osm_names_v   = list(split_clean(osm_names)),
    osm_refs_v    = list(split_clean(osm_refs)),
    snd_concats_v = list(split_clean(snd_ordstnameconcats)),
    label = paste0("[", corridor_idx, "] ",
                   coalesce(osm_names, osm_refs, snd_ordstnameconcats))
  ) |>
  ungroup()

cat("Loaded", nrow(corridors), "corridors\n")
print(dplyr::select(corridors, corridor_idx, osm_names, osm_refs,
                    snd_ordstnameconcats))
```

## 2. Load OSM streetnet (cached)

`StreetSetup.Rmd` writes an `sf` LineString layer of all driveable OSM ways in the PSRC 4-county clip to `outputs/streets/osm_streetnet.rds`. Columns we need: `osm_id`, `name`, `ref`, `oneway`, `highway`, plus geometry.

```{r load-osm}
stopifnot(file.exists(params$streetnet_rds))
streetnet <- readRDS(params$streetnet_rds)

# Force osm_id to character WITHOUT going through any numeric coercion.
# `osmextract` sometimes returns osm_id as double / integer64, and OSM
# IDs for modern features exceed 2^31; once they touch `double` precision
# the trailing digits get rounded. `format(., scientific = FALSE, trim
# = TRUE)` handles double safely (suppresses 1.23e+18 output), and the
# `bit64` path handles 64-bit ints. If osm_id is already character this
# is a no-op.
.osm_id_to_char <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "integer64")) {
    if (!requireNamespace("bit64", quietly = TRUE)) {
      stop("streetnet osm_id is integer64 but the 'bit64' package isn't ",
           "available — install it or rebuild the streetnet with osm_id ",
           "as character.")
    }
    bit64::as.character.integer64(x)
  } else if (is.numeric(x)) {
    .scipen_old <- getOption("scipen")
    options(scipen = 1000)
    on.exit(options(scipen = .scipen_old), add = TRUE)
    format(x, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
  } else {
    as.character(x)
  }
}
.cls_before <- paste(class(streetnet$osm_id), collapse = ",")
streetnet$osm_id <- .osm_id_to_char(streetnet$osm_id)
cat(sprintf("streetnet$osm_id coerced %s → character\n", .cls_before))

# Some PBF rows have NA name and NA ref (residential connectors) — they
# can't be in any corridor, so drop them up front to shrink subsequent work.
streetnet <- streetnet[!is.na(streetnet$name) | !is.na(streetnet$ref), ]
cat("OSM ways with a name or ref:", nrow(streetnet), "\n")

streetnet_p <- sf::st_transform(streetnet, params$planar_crs)
```

## 3. Load Seattle Streets + SND directional rows

SDOT Seattle Streets provides per-COMPKEY linestring geometry; the SND CSV gives the directional (COMPKEY × SND_ID × TRAFFICDIR) row set. Joining the two by `COMPKEY` lets us look up geometry for any SND row.

```{r load-snd}
streets <- sf::st_read(params$streets_geojson, quiet = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(COMPKEY, STNAME_ORD, SEGDIR, ONEWAY, ONEWAYDIR) |>
  mutate(COMPKEY = as.integer(COMPKEY)) |>
  sf::st_transform(params$planar_crs)
cat("Seattle Streets features:", nrow(streets), "\n")

snd <- readr::read_csv(params$snd_csv,
                       show_col_types = FALSE,
                       progress = FALSE) |>
  transmute(
    COMPKEY     = suppressWarnings(as.integer(COMPKEY)),
    SND_ID      = suppressWarnings(as.integer(SND_ID)),
    TRAFFICDIR  = toupper(stringr::str_trim(as.character(TRAFFICDIR))),
    STNAME_ORD,
    SND_ORD_STNAME_CONCAT,
    OSM_WAY_ID = as.character(OSM_WAY_ID)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(COMPKEY), !is.na(SND_ID), !is.na(TRAFFICDIR))
cat("SND directional rows:", nrow(snd), "\n")
```

## 4. Matching helpers

```{r helpers}
CARDINAL_BEARING <- c(N =   0, NE = 45,  E = 90,  SE = 135,
                      S = 180, SW = 225, W = 270, NW = 315)

# Length-weighted mean bearing of a single LineString (planar coords).
# Returns NA for zero-length / degenerate geometry.
mean_bearing_planar <- function(line) {
  m <- sf::st_coordinates(line)
  if (nrow(m) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  dx <- diff(m[, "X"])
  dy <- diff(m[, "Y"])
  seg_len <- sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)
  if (sum(seg_len) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  # Bearing in degrees clockwise from north for each sub-segment.
  brng <- (90 - atan2(dy, dx) * 180 / pi) %% 360
  # Mean as sum of unit vectors weighted by segment length, then atan2.
  vx <- sum(seg_len * sin(brng * pi / 180))
  vy <- sum(seg_len * cos(brng * pi / 180))
  (atan2(vx, vy) * 180 / pi) %% 360
}

# Angular distance in degrees between two bearings (0-180).
angular_dist <- function(a, b) {
  d <- abs((a - b + 180) %% 360 - 180)
  d
}

# OSM `oneway` tag → logical. Accepts "yes", "true", "1" as true;
# "no", "false", "0", NA, "" as false. "-1" (reverse oneway) means
# the OSM geometry is reversed wrt traffic — we still treat it as
# directional, but `mean_bearing_planar` of the geometry needs
# flipping before comparing to SND TRAFFICDIR.
parse_oneway <- function(x) {
  x <- tolower(stringr::str_trim(as.character(x)))
  x[is.na(x) | x == ""] <- params$default_oneway
  dplyr::case_when(
    x %in% c("yes", "true", "1") ~ "yes",
    x == "-1"                     ~ "reverse",
    TRUE                          ~ "no"
  )
}

# For an OSM ref like "I 5;US 99", split on ";" and trim.
split_osm_ref <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return(character(0))
  toupper(stringr::str_trim(strsplit(as.character(x), ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]))
}
```

## 5. Per-corridor matching

For each corridor:

* Filter OSM to features whose `name` is in the corridor's name list **or** whose `ref` contains any of the corridor's ref values.
* Filter SND to rows whose `SND_ORD_STNAME_CONCAT` is in the corridor's list; pull geometry for those COMPKEYs.
* For each OSM way: sample a point every `sample_spacing_m` along its length, find the nearest in-corridor COMPKEY for each point (capped at `max_sample_dist_m`), and keep the set of unique COMPKEYs it touches.
* Assign direction: if OSM is `oneway=yes`, match the way's length-weighted bearing to the closest SND `TRAFFICDIR` cardinal for that COMPKEY; if `oneway=-1`, do the same after flipping; if not one-way, attach to every TRAFFICDIR row for that COMPKEY.
* Emit one row per `(COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR, way_id)` triple.

```{r match-fn}
match_one_corridor <- function(crow, n_total) {
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  cat(sprintf("\n[%d/%d] %s\n", crow$corridor_idx, n_total, crow$label))
  flush.console()

  # ---------- (a) OSM filter ----------
  names_v <- crow$osm_names_v[[1]]
  refs_v  <- crow$osm_refs_v[[1]]

  osm_name_hit <- if (length(names_v))
    !is.na(streetnet_p$name) & toupper(streetnet_p$name) %in% names_v
  else rep(FALSE, nrow(streetnet_p))

  osm_ref_hit <- if (length(refs_v)) {
    vapply(streetnet_p$ref, function(r) {
      any(split_osm_ref(r) %in% refs_v)
    }, logical(1))
  } else rep(FALSE, nrow(streetnet_p))

  osm_sub <- streetnet_p[osm_name_hit | osm_ref_hit, ]
  cat("  OSM ways matched (name+ref):", nrow(osm_sub), "\n")
  if (nrow(osm_sub) == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("  done (%.1fs) — no OSM ways matched, skipping\n",
                as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")))
    return(tibble())
  }

  # ---------- (b) SND filter ----------
  concats_v <- crow$snd_concats_v[[1]]
  snd_sub <- snd |>
    filter(toupper(stringr::str_trim(SND_ORD_STNAME_CONCAT)) %in% concats_v)
  cat("  SND rows matched (SND_ORD_STNAME_CONCAT):", nrow(snd_sub), "\n")
  if (nrow(snd_sub) == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("  done (%.1fs) — no SND rows matched, skipping\n",
                as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")))
    return(tibble())
  }

  compkeys_in_corridor <- unique(snd_sub$COMPKEY)
  streets_sub <- streets[streets$COMPKEY %in% compkeys_in_corridor, ]
  cat("  Seattle Streets COMPKEYs available:",
      nrow(streets_sub), "of", length(compkeys_in_corridor), "\n")
  if (nrow(streets_sub) == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("  done (%.1fs) — no COMPKEY geometry, skipping\n",
                as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")))
    return(tibble())
  }

  # ---------- (c) Sample OSM ways and snap to SND ----------
  # Number of samples per OSM way: enough to cover its length at
  # roughly `sample_spacing_m` between points (min 2).
  osm_len <- as.numeric(sf::st_length(osm_sub))
  n_samples <- pmax(2L, as.integer(ceiling(osm_len / params$sample_spacing_m)))

  # `st_line_sample` accepts a vector `n` (one value per LineString) and
  # returns an sfc of MULTIPOINTs. Cast to POINT to explode into one row
  # per sample, with `osm_row` carrying the originating OSM way.
  sample_geom <- sf::st_line_sample(osm_sub, n = n_samples)
  sample_sf <- sf::st_sf(osm_row = seq_len(nrow(osm_sub)),
                         geometry = sample_geom,
                         crs = sf::st_crs(osm_sub))
  pts_sf <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_cast(sample_sf, "POINT"))
  cat("  OSM sample points:", nrow(pts_sf), "\n")

  # Nearest COMPKEY per sample point.
  nearest_idx <- sf::st_nearest_feature(pts_sf, streets_sub)
  nearest_dist <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(
    pts_sf, streets_sub[nearest_idx, ], by_element = TRUE))

  hits_all <- tibble(
    osm_row  = pts_sf$osm_row,
    COMPKEY  = streets_sub$COMPKEY[nearest_idx],
    dist_m   = nearest_dist
  )

  # Strict-tolerance hits (preferred).
  hits_close <- hits_all |>
    filter(dist_m <= params$max_sample_dist_m)

  # Fallback: ways that produced ZERO close hits keep their nearest snaps
  # up to `max_sample_dist_fallback_m`. The name/ref filter has already
  # restricted us to ways belonging to this corridor, so a farther-away
  # snap is still informative (e.g. SR-99 Tunnel: OSM geometry runs
  # underground, SDOT geometry runs at street level, but they're the same
  # corridor segment).
  ways_with_close_hits <- unique(hits_close$osm_row)
  ways_missing <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(osm_sub)), ways_with_close_hits)
  hits_far <- if (length(ways_missing)) {
    hits_all |>
      filter(osm_row %in% ways_missing,
             dist_m <= params$max_sample_dist_fallback_m)
  } else {
    hits_all[0, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  if (nrow(hits_far) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("  fallback snap: %d ways had no hit within %.0fm; using nearest within %.0fm (%d points)\n",
                length(unique(hits_far$osm_row)),
                params$max_sample_dist_m,
                params$max_sample_dist_fallback_m,
                nrow(hits_far)))
  }

  hits <- dplyr::bind_rows(hits_close, hits_far)

  if (nrow(hits) == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("  done (%.1fs) — no sample points within max_sample_dist_fallback_m\n",
                as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")))
    return(tibble())
  }

  # For each OSM way, list the unique COMPKEYs it touches and their
  # representative (nearest) distance, used for diagnostics only.
  per_way_compkeys <- hits |>
    group_by(osm_row, COMPKEY) |>
    summarise(min_dist_m = min(dist_m), n_pts = n(),
              .groups = "drop")
  cat("  unique (OSM × COMPKEY) hits:", nrow(per_way_compkeys), "\n")

  # ---------- (d) OSM way attributes (way_id, bearing, oneway) ----------
  osm_attrs <- tibble(
    osm_row = seq_len(nrow(osm_sub)),
    way_id  = as.character(osm_sub$osm_id),
    oneway  = parse_oneway(osm_sub$oneway),
    bearing = vapply(seq_len(nrow(osm_sub)),
                     function(i) mean_bearing_planar(osm_sub$geometry[i]),
                     numeric(1))
  ) |>
    # `oneway=-1` means OSM geometry is reversed wrt traffic, so flip
    # the bearing 180° before any TRAFFICDIR comparison.
    mutate(bearing = if_else(oneway == "reverse",
                             (bearing + 180) %% 360,
                             bearing),
           oneway_logical = oneway %in% c("yes", "reverse"))

  per_way_compkeys <- per_way_compkeys |>
    left_join(osm_attrs, by = "osm_row")

  # ---------- (e) Direction inference ----------
  # For each (OSM way × COMPKEY) hit, look up the SND rows available for
  # that COMPKEY (one per TRAFFICDIR). For oneway OSM, pick the single
  # closest TRAFFICDIR by cardinal bearing distance. For non-oneway OSM,
  # emit one row per TRAFFICDIR.
  snd_by_ck <- snd_sub |>
    select(COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR) |>
    distinct()

  out <- per_way_compkeys |>
    inner_join(snd_by_ck, by = "COMPKEY",
               relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    mutate(td_bearing = unname(CARDINAL_BEARING[TRAFFICDIR]),
           bearing_gap = if_else(oneway_logical & !is.na(bearing) & !is.na(td_bearing),
                                 angular_dist(bearing, td_bearing),
                                 NA_real_)) |>
    group_by(osm_row, COMPKEY) |>
    mutate(
      keep = if (any(oneway_logical) && !all(is.na(bearing_gap))) {
        # One-way OSM: pick the single closest TRAFFICDIR for this COMPKEY,
        # but only if the bearing is actually aligned (<90° off). A larger
        # gap means the OSM way is heading the wrong way for every
        # TRAFFICDIR present on this COMPKEY — typically an SND-divided
        # case where the sample point happened to snap to the opposite-
        # direction COMPKEY across the median. Drop those rather than
        # emit a contradictory mapping.
        is_min <- bearing_gap == min(bearing_gap, na.rm = TRUE) &
                  !is.na(bearing_gap)
        is_min & bearing_gap < 90
      } else {
        # Two-way OSM: attach to every TRAFFICDIR of the COMPKEY.
        rep(TRUE, dplyr::n())
      }
    ) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(keep) |>
    transmute(COMPKEY = as.integer(COMPKEY),
              SND_ID = as.integer(SND_ID),
              TRAFFICDIR,
              way_id,
              osm_oneway = oneway,
              osm_bearing = bearing,
              td_bearing,
              bearing_gap,
              min_sample_dist_m = min_dist_m,
              corridor_idx = crow$corridor_idx,
              corridor_label = crow$label)

  # Per-corridor coverage diagnostic.
  covered_ck <- length(unique(out$COMPKEY))
  missing_ck <- setdiff(compkeys_in_corridor, out$COMPKEY)
  cat(sprintf("  COMPKEYs covered: %d / %d (missing %d)\n",
              covered_ck, length(compkeys_in_corridor), length(missing_ck)))
  if (length(missing_ck) > 0 && length(missing_ck) <= 20) {
    cat("    missing:", paste(missing_ck, collapse = ","), "\n")
  }
  cat(sprintf("  done (%.1fs) — emitted %d rows\n",
              as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs"),
              nrow(out)))
  out
}

cat("\nProcessing", nrow(corridors), "corridors...\n")
t_all <- Sys.time()
results <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(corridors)), function(i) {
  match_one_corridor(corridors[i, ], n_total = nrow(corridors))
})
cat(sprintf("\nAll %d corridors done in %.1fs. Total hits: %d\n",
            nrow(corridors),
            as.numeric(Sys.time() - t_all, units = "secs"),
            nrow(results)))
```

## 6. Build the repair table

Collapse to one row per `(COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR)` with comma-separated `WAY_IDS`. A given way_id may legitimately appear in multiple rows (a long OSM way that spans many SND COMPKEYs); a given `(COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR)` triple may legitimately have multiple way_ids (a short SND segment hit by multiple OSM features at a transition).

```{r build-repair}
repair_long <- results |>
  distinct(COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR, way_id)

# Sanity: drop rows where any key column ended up NA.
n_drop <- sum(is.na(repair_long$COMPKEY) | is.na(repair_long$SND_ID) |
              is.na(repair_long$TRAFFICDIR) | is.na(repair_long$way_id))
if (n_drop > 0) {
  cat("Dropping", n_drop, "rows with NA in key columns\n")
  repair_long <- repair_long |>
    filter(!is.na(COMPKEY), !is.na(SND_ID),
           !is.na(TRAFFICDIR), !is.na(way_id))
}

repair_wide <- repair_long |>
  arrange(COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR, way_id) |>
  group_by(COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR) |>
  summarise(WAY_IDS = paste(way_id, collapse = ","), .groups = "drop")

cat("Repair rows (triples):", nrow(repair_wide), "\n")
cat("Repair rows (way_id-level):", nrow(repair_long), "\n")
cat("Distinct way_ids in repair:", length(unique(repair_long$way_id)), "\n")

dir.create(dirname(params$repair_csv), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# `quote = "all"` forces every cell to be quoted, including WAY_IDS values
# that happen to be all-digits when there's only one way_id per triple.
# Without this, readr's type inference reads the column as numeric on
# subsequent reads, which (a) loses precision for OSM IDs > 2^53 via
# scientific notation, and (b) eats the commas in multi-way_id rows,
# silently breaking the part-2 §4c override. quote = "all" makes the CSV
# unambiguously character on round-trip.
readr::write_csv(repair_wide, params$repair_csv, quote = "all")
cat("Wrote:", normalizePath(params$repair_csv), "\n")
```
